summary.headline: Aegis Logistics H1 FY27 PAT doubled to INR866 crore on 97% EBITDA growth to INR1,184 crore, alongside an $809 million Tristar acquisition.
summary.overview: Aegis Logistics reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR2,213 crore (down from INR2,294 crore), with normalized segment EBITDA up 32% to INR456 crore and PAT up 32% to INR321 crore. H1 FY27 PAT rose 108% to INR866 crore and EBITDA nearly doubled to INR1,184 crore, led by the Gas (LPG) division. Management signed a definitive agreement on 13 October 2026 to acquire 89.8% of Tristar Holdings for US$809 million, with completion expected in Q4 FY27. Aegis Vopak Terminals (AVTL) posted Q2 revenue up about 17% and EBITDA up 22%, but PAT fell to INR96 crore on higher finance and tax costs.

segments.name: Gas (LPG) Division
segments.commentary: Q2 EBITDA INR309.25 crore (+34% YoY); H1 EBITDA INR900 crore (+137%). Distribution volumes 2.41 lakh MT in Q2 and 5.18 lakh MT in H1; distribution EBITDA per ton about INR7,000 in Q2, which management called a normal quarter.

segments.name: Liquid Division
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR187 crore (+21%) and EBITDA INR147 crore (+27%); H1 EBITDA margin about 78%. Realization above INR3,600 per CBM on 2 million CBM storage; management expects about INR3,000 per CBM EBITDA this year.

segments.name: Logistics / Sourcing
segments.commentary: Q2 logistics throughput 1.34 million MT, down 5% YoY but up 19% QoQ after a geopolitics-hit Q1. Sourcing volumes 0.9 lakh MT in Q2 and 2.1 lakh MT in H1, lower on expired contracts.

segments.name: Aegis Vopak Terminals (AVTL)
segments.commentary: Q2 EBITDA INR212 crore (+22%) with margin 78.6%; PAT INR96.4 crore (down from INR100.2 crore) on higher finance cost and tax. Cumulative capex about USD 1.2 billion by next year; about USD 5 billion planned through FY2030-31.

guidance_outlook: Tristar acquisition (89.8% for US$809 million, signed 13 October 2026) expected to complete in Q4 FY27, subject to regulatory approvals; synergy details deferred until closing.
Management expects the second half to be as good as or better than H1; next update expected around end-January.
Distribution volumes on track to approach 1 million MT for FY27 based on H1 run-rate.
Ammonia take-or-pay contract with Hindustan Zinc (15 years) expected to start later in FY27.
Funding: EGM approval for INR6,000 crore; about INR6,400 crore cash on September balance sheet; AVTL gearing target no more than 0.6x.
capex_capacity: JNPT: first phase of about 100,000 CBM liquid storage (part of 318,000 CBM greenfield, INR1,675 crore total incl. about 77,286 MT LPG) to commission in Q3 FY27; LPG bottling plant (35,000 MT) commissioned 15 October 2026.
Mumbai: additional 64,000 CBM liquid storage at INR125 crore, progressing on schedule with gradual commissioning this year.
Kochi: 49,577 CBM expansion to take total to 132,000 CBM, commissioning early FY28.
Kandla: CRL-4 liquid terminal adding 94,148 CBM, commissioning targeted next financial year; Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline about 96% physically complete (1,958 km trunk laid).

Pipavav ammonia terminal (36,000 MT) commissioned, built at about USD 50 million (about INR525 crore); ITOCHU holds 10% of Aegis Terminal Pipavav, targeting 25% over three years. Mangalore: 75,000 CBM added and at 100% utilization, total 193,000 CBM; evaluating 60,000 CBM more.
demand_pricing: LPG distribution margin about INR7,000 per ton in Q2, versus about INR4,000-7,000 historically; management attributes margin to procurement and freight efficiency, not price setting.
Management claims more than 30% of India's static LPG storage capacity; current throughput capacity about 20 million tons, with 29 million tons targeted once JNPT is ready.
Ammonia: CRISIL-cited supply-demand gap of about 3 million tons by 2029; storage charge about INR2,750 per MT; management targets about INR10,000 per MT total revenue potential.
Liquid realization above INR3,600 per CBM; AVTL reported lower Liquid realization QoQ but higher margins from JNPT mix.

qa_highlights.question: Integration challenges from Tristar acquisition given geographic and segment differences?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tristar has operated for 30 years, its entire management will stay, and Aegis will add its skill set without disrupting operations.

qa_highlights.question: Synergies from Tristar for Aegis Logistics, e.g., procurement or input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing the deal not being complete; cited overlapping liquid and gas storage, shipping, trucks and distribution skills. Details promised after closing.

qa_highlights.question: Is LPG distribution margin returning to INR7,000 per ton, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 margin about INR7,000 per ton; Q1 had geopolitics-driven price margins. Margin driven by cost efficiency from larger terminals and supply chain partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: Market share and growth drivers for LPG?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 30% of India's static LPG capacity; growth drivers cited as income-led energy demand, shift from solid fuels, and large-vessel unloading cost advantages.

qa_highlights.question: Ammonia demand clarity and contribution outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Referred to CRISIL-cited supply gap of about 3 million tons by 2029; plans vertical integration across sourcing, storage and distribution, with distribution margin similar to LPG at about INR7,000 per ton.

qa_highlights.question: How will the about USD 5 billion AVTL capex and USD 809 million Tristar deal be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Tristar funded from about INR6,400 crore cash, within the INR6,000 crore EGM-approved funding; AVTL capex funded by equity from IPO dilution, internal accruals and debt at no more than 0.6x gearing, with about USD 2 billion equity needed.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity in LPG terminals (Petronet, IOCL, BPCL, JSW Infra)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India has about 1 million MT static storage, under 10 days' cover, so new infrastructure is welcome if built at the right cost and time.

risks_watch: Tristar acquisition (89.8%, US$809 million): completion expected Q4 FY27 subject to regulatory approvals; management withheld synergy quantification until closing.

LPG distribution margin sustainability: about INR7,000 per ton in Q2 versus INR4,000-7,000 historically; management says it follows rather than sets price, so margin depends on procurement and freight efficiency.

Commissioning timelines: JNPT first 100,000 CBM phase in Q3 FY27, Kochi expansion early FY28, Kandla CRL-4 next FY, Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline about 96% complete, Mumbai 64,000 CBM gradual through the year.
Ammonia take-or-pay (Hindustan Zinc, 15 years) start later in FY27; ammonia demand relies on CRISIL-cited supply gap of about 3 million tons by 2029.
Funding load: about USD 5 billion AVTL capex through FY2030-31 at 0.6x gearing needs about USD 2 billion equity; AVTL Q2 PAT fell YoY on higher finance cost and tax.
Logistics throughput recovery: Q2 1.34 million MT still down 5% YoY; sourcing volumes lower on expired contracts. Next update expected around end-January.
key_quotes: So on the 13th of October 2026, we signed a definitive agreement to acquire 89.8% stake in Tristar Holdings Limited for a consideration of US$809 million.
We don't expect to change the management and the continuity will ensure that there is no disturbance in the operations and performance of the company.
So we hold more than 30% of the static capacity of LPG in the country.
So we are -- Aegis Vopak capex is self-funded by dilution of equity and listing of its shares.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on operating performance, calling Q2 a perfect quarter and expecting H2 to be as good or better than H1. Guarded on Tristar, repeatedly declining to quantify synergies or deal benefits until closing.

adds.what: JNPT first phase ~100,000 CBM liquid storage (part of 318,000 CBM greenfield)
Kandla-Gorakhpur LPG pipeline (1,958 km trunk), ~96% physically complete

growth.why: Management expects H2 to be as good as or better than H1 and distribution volumes to approach 1 million MT in FY27, backed by JNPT phase 1 (~100,000 CBM, Q3 FY27), Mumbai, Kochi and Kandla capacity and the Hindustan Zinc ammonia contract, though no revenue growth % was guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Liquid division EBITDA margin about 78% in H1 and management expects about INR3,000 per CBM EBITDA this year; LPG distribution margin about INR7,000 per ton in Q2 versus INR4,000-7,000 historically, though management says it follows rather than sets price.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: JNPT first phase of about 100,000 CBM liquid storage commissions in Q3 FY27, Mumbai adds 64,000 CBM gradually through FY27, Kochi 49,577 CBM in early FY28, and Kandla CRL-4 adds 94,148 CBM next FY; Kandla-Gorakhpur pipeline about 96% complete.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Distribution volume 2.41 lakh MT in Q2 (+25% YoY) and 5.18 lakh MT in H1 (+54%), with management guiding to approach 1 million MT in FY27; utilisation is only about 25%, so volume growth depends on new capacity coming live rather than existing assets.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management raised its aggregate capex plan to about USD 5 billion through FY2030-31 and about USD 2 billion of equity is still needed, with Mangalore evaluating 60,000 CBM more; further project announcements are expected even though current utilisation is only about 25%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects H2 to be as good as or better than H1 after H1 PAT of INR866 crore (+108%), but no revenue growth % was guided and H2 has not been quantified.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 logistics throughput was still down 5% YoY, the LPG margin of about INR7,000 per ton is above the INR4,000-7,000 historical range and driven by procurement and freight efficiency, and Mumbai commissioning was cut to gradual timing; Tristar completion depends on regulatory approvals.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Ammonia take-or-pay contract with Hindustan Zinc (15 years) starts later in FY27 on the 36,000 MT Pipavav ammonia terminal, and management targets about INR10,000 per MT total ammonia revenue potential.

rows.label: Tristar Holdings acquisition (89.8% for US$809 million)
rows.why: Definitive agreement signed 13 October 2026, funded from about INR6,400 crore cash within the INR6,000 crore EGM-approved funding; completion subject to regulatory approvals, with synergies not quantified.

rows.label: Hindustan Zinc ammonia take-or-pay (15 years)
rows.why: Contract is firm for 15 years and start is guided for later in FY27, backing the ammonia storage ramp at Pipavav.

rows.label: AVTL gearing held at no more than 0.6x
rows.why: AVTL PAT fell to INR96.4 crore in Q2 from INR100.2 crore on higher finance cost and tax, so gearing discipline is needed while about USD 5 billion capex proceeds.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating performance, calling Q2 a perfect quarter and guiding H2 at least as good as H1, while staying guarded on Tristar synergies and declining to quantify them until closing; analysts pressed on the Tristar integration, synergies and funding.
